_about: Tunables for scripts/security/dast_ingress_sweep.py (ADR 0155, increment 2, ingress plane). Every floor is a MINIMUM with headroom under a measured value; below one the run exits 2 (could not measure), never 0. Every resource bound is a MAXIMUM with headroom over a measured value. Raise a floor when the real number grows; NEVER lower a floor or raise a bound to make a run pass.

_provenance.measured: 2026-09-26 on Windows 11 against branch b100-dast-ingress (origin/main 58f15e31f merged with ddbfc16a6), seed 318, 24 mutations
_provenance.remeasured_why: The first measurement the same day (mllp 57 cases, 81 frames, 41 NAKs) was taken before the code review corrected the mutation corpus (a sentinel-bearing seed added, X12 mutations kept off the ISA) and the at-cap case (it was one byte over). Those numbers were a property of the old corpus, so the floors were re-cut from this measurement, not lowered to pass a run.
_provenance.cases_per_plane: measured mllp 58 (40 catalogue + 18 mutations), tcp 9, x12 15 (9 catalogue + 6 mutations)
_provenance.min_frames_decoded: measured tcp 7 and x12 9 (6 catalogue + 3 mutation)
_provenance.min_mllp_rejected_replies: measured 10 in the catalogue (14 with mutations) after merging engine PR 1583, up from 8, because both blank-segment frames now get a NAK; the floor sits at the catalogue's own 10 so a mutation draw cannot trip it
_provenance.min_log_records_seen: measured 32 INFO+ engine records; the floor only proves the watch was fed
_provenance.resource_bounds: measured heap growth between -50695 and +19628 bytes, handles +0 to +2, tasks +0 over 2 passes across four runs; the leak canary measured heap +8413697 and handles +32
_provenance.wall_seconds: measured about 7 for the seeded run
_provenance.budget_headroom: measured 2026-09-26 on a 20-core Windows 11 box already near full CPU, six runs, three of them beside a pytest -n 8 run: the slowest half-close close was 0.36s against case_seconds 5.0, the slowest stall close 1.02s against stall_close_seconds 3.0, the slowest settle 0.026s against settle_seconds 3.0, the slowest connect 0.002s against connect_seconds 1.0. Yet merge-group run 36242551283 (windows-2022, full suite) saw one raw-TCP pipelined-three case take more than 5.0s to close in the traced resource phase, so a hosted runner's tail is at least 14 times this box's worst. That is why the required leg runs the 'required' profile below.

profiles._about: A profile raises wall-clock bounds in 'budget' and nothing else; the sweep refuses any other key and any value below the strict one. With no --profile the strict budget above applies, and that is what the advisory nightly (dast.yml) runs. 'required' is what tests/test_dast_ingress_sweep.py runs inside the required pytest legs, where a loaded hosted runner has stalled one close past 5s: each bound there is five or six times the strict one, so only a listener that never closes, or one far slower than any load seen, is reported. It costs nothing on a healthy run, because every wait ends when the listener closes. The stall canary keeps its own canary.case_seconds under any profile, and the stall control in the test waits out the full required stall_close_seconds, so both halves of the time detector are still proven to fire under this profile.

known_defects.blank-segment: Engine defect 1 in ADR 0155's 2026-09-26 amendment, which is the one place its current behaviour is stated. Tolerated only when the frame the inbound handler faulted on carries a blank segment. Pinned by strict xfails in tests/test_dast_ingress_sweep.py.
known_defects.alphanumeric-field-separator: Engine defect found by this pass on 2026-09-26: a message whose MSH-1 is a letter or digit is accepted, and the ACK echoes that separator, so MSA-1 (AA/AE/AR, themselves letters) cannot be read back by the sender. Pinned by a strict xfail in tests/test_dast_ingress_sweep.py.

canary._cases_note: listener-down runs only the first two: every probe after the stop costs connect_seconds, and two refused probes plus one refused case already clear its floor.
